explanation: The faster a vehicle travels on a wet road, the less time tire treads have to channel water away from the contact patch, so hydroplaning and skidding risk rises directly with speed.

When ABS engages during hard braking it rapidly pulses the brakes many times a second to stop the wheels locking, which the driver feels as vibration and hears as noise through the pedal - a normal sign the system is working.
Fog mainly degrades a driver's ability to see the road, other vehicles, and hazards at a distance, which is why vision, rather than acceleration, braking, or steering, is the ability most impaired.
Fatigue-related accidents stem from a drop in the driver's own level of alertness, and that drop can happen on any type of road, not only on winding roads or steep grades.

The duty to keep a safe following gap requires enough space from vehicles ahead and alongside so that sudden braking, swerving, or lane changes by a vehicle traveling the same direction can still be avoided safely.
By standard dashboard-telltale convention, a blue warning light specifically indicates the high-beam headlights are switched on, distinguishing it from the low-beam and parking-light indicators.

The legal minimum following gap is based on having enough space to brake safely, and that minimum of not less than one second applies regardless of the size of the vehicle ahead, not some multiplied distance just because it is a truck.

Tread grooves exist mainly to channel water out from between the tire and the road surface, preventing a water film from building up and so preserving the tire's friction and contact with the road on wet surfaces.
Regulation 99(a) requires dimming the high beam because its intensity can dazzle (temporarily blind) oncoming or leading drivers, creating a serious hazard for everyone on the road.
Sidewalks are reserved for pedestrians, and bypassing a road obstruction is not one of the narrow legal exceptions that allow a motor vehicle onto the sidewalk, so it remains prohibited.
Portable flashing warning boards of this type are placed to alert approaching drivers to roadwork ahead, giving advance notice before they reach the actual worksite.

To keep taxis, which carry paying passengers, in a properly roadworthy condition, the law bars issuing or renewing a taxi's registration once the vehicle is more than 12 years past its manufacture date.

A lit brake-system warning lamp signals a possible fault in the vehicle's most safety-critical system, so the duty of care requires stopping and discontinuing the drive rather than risking unreliable brakes.
The person in control of the vehicle at the time is legally responsible for its roadworthiness and for keeping its emissions within the statutory limit while it is being driven.
The general duty of care requires adapting speed to road-surface conditions, and a rough road calls for slowing down and heightened alertness to keep control and react to sudden bumps or hazards.
A utility tractor's vehicle registration document specifies its approved passenger capacity, so carrying an extra passenger is only lawful when that document expressly permits it.

Taking one hand off the wheel is only accepted for brief mechanical actions needed to operate the vehicle, such as shifting gears, not for tasks like phone calls or texting that meaningfully divert attention from driving.

A left U-turn at an intersection without traffic lights is permitted only when it causes no obstruction to other traffic, the driver has a clear view in all directions, and no road sign specifically prohibits it.

Loss of vehicle control typically results from several factors combining together - excessive speed reduces the margin for error, low vigilance delays noticing a hazard, and unfamiliarity with the vehicle makes correcting a mistake harder.

Sedatives impair reaction time and judgment much like alcohol or drugs, so driving under their influence is barred unless the medication's own prescription explicitly states it doesn't affect fitness to drive.

The auxiliary (parking/hand) brake's defined purpose is to hold a stationary vehicle in place and stop it rolling, separate from the service (foot) brake that is used to slow or stop the vehicle while it is moving.
Coasting downhill in neutral disconnects the engine's braking effect and reduces the driver's control over speed, which is why the law explicitly forbids it as dangerous.

A road accident is legally defined as an unintentional event resulting in injury to anyone, including the driver, or in property damage, or both, not a deliberate act or one limited to a single kind of victim.
The maximum speed table sets buses other than minibuses at 100 km/h on a freeway, lower than the 110 km/h allowed for private cars, reflecting the bus's size and the safety of its passengers.
The legal definition of a private bus turns on its use rather than ownership: it is any bus that does not operate as a public service (fare-paying passenger transport) vehicle.
Because carrying paying passengers involves added responsibility, the Licensing Authority sets the minimum age for a Public Service Vehicle license at 21, higher than the general minimum driving age.
A Class B license covers motor vehicles up to 3,500 kg gross weight, which includes a privately used minibus within that limit, but not a public or commercial minibus, which needs separate licensing.
The clutch lever's mechanical function is to disengage the engine from the gearbox, which is what allows the rider to change gears without stalling the engine.
The special bicycle-path signal lights follow a fixed, prescribed order set out in the official traffic-sign chart, and in that sequence sign 716 is immediately followed by sign 708.
A modified pressure exhaust increases engine noise beyond the permitted limit, and equipment rules bar this on motorcycles just as on any other vehicle, regardless of who installed it.
Following the fixed, prescribed order of the special bicycle-path signal chart, sign 710 is immediately followed by sign 716 in the sequence.

To ensure the certifying doctor has enough firsthand knowledge of the applicant's health history to judge fitness to drive, the regulation requires the examining physician to have treated that applicant for at least three years.

If a motorcycle's foot (rear) brake fails, the rider should slow down using the hand-operated front brake together with downshifting to lower gears for engine braking, since these remain available controls.
A rough non-urban road reduces tire grip and control, especially on a two-wheeled vehicle, so the safe response is to slow down to avoid losing control rather than maintaining or increasing speed.

Turning right at an unmarked junction doesn't cross the path of a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction, so the driver may proceed carefully without being required to stop and yield, unlike a left turn across oncoming traffic.
Responsibility for a vehicle parked in a prohibited area rests with the registered owner by default, unless that owner can identify the actual driver who committed the offense at the time.
The statutory no-parking zone around a pedestrian crossing covers both the crossing itself and the 12 meters immediately before it, keeping drivers' and pedestrians' sightlines clear.

The duty of care requires extra caution around a vehicle unloading children, since a child may step into the road unpredictably, so slowing to a low speed is the correct response rather than overtaking quickly.
When a vehicle ahead signals it is turning left, it will be moving toward the left side of the road, leaving its right side clear, so overtaking on the right is the safe and permitted option.
Pushing a vehicle, even with the engine off, counts legally as driving it, so all restrictions on entering a road where vehicle entry is prohibited still apply.
At an intersection without traffic signs, the default right-of-way rule requires yielding to any vehicle approaching from your right, the basic priority rule used when no other rule or sign applies.
The default rule is that a U-turn is permitted from any lane, and it is only barred where a specific traffic sign or marking prohibits it.
An unbroken separation line paired with a dashed line to its left marks a protected separation area, and crossing this combined marking remains forbidden regardless of the dashed portion.

An Electronic Stability Program compares the driver's intended path from the steering input against the vehicle's actual path in real time and corrects the mismatch, which is what prevents loss of control while skidding.

Overtaking a vehicle that is legitimately using the hard shoulder is allowed from the normal lane provided the overtaking vehicle stays within its own lane and doesn't cross the solid separation line with any wheel.
Hard shoulders are set aside specifically for hand-propelled vehicles, tractors, and other slow-moving vehicles that would otherwise hold up the traffic behind them, not for general vehicle use.

Overtaking before a pedestrian crossing is barred universally, on every type of road, because it blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the exact point where they need to see each other.
The statutory no-parking distance before a pedestrian crossing is 12 meters, keeping the approach to the crossing clear for both drivers' and pedestrians' visibility.
Under the Ministry of Transportation's regulatory structure, the Inspector of Transport is the specific authority empowered to issue permits for operating a bus service.
A steady (non-flashing) yellow light follows green and precedes red, so it signals the driver to prepare to stop, or to clear the intersection immediately if already too close to stop safely.

Even with a green light, entering an intersection whose exit is blocked is prohibited, since doing so would leave the vehicle stranded across the junction and obstruct cross traffic once the light changes - the anti-gridlock rule.

On a narrow roadway where two opposing vehicles cannot pass at once, both drivers must keep as far right as possible, even onto the hard shoulder, since neither vehicle has an automatic right of way in that situation.
To keep the crossing and its approach clear for a train or for vehicles negotiating it, the law prohibits stopping or parking within at least 20 meters before or after a level crossing.
A rear camera's stated purpose is to show the driver the blind spots directly behind the vehicle, which is why it is used mainly for reversing.
Unless a sign states otherwise, the default speed limit for private passenger cars on urban roads is 50 km/h, as set out in the maximum-speed regulations.

Once the advance level-crossing sign appears roughly 100 meters before the crossing, overtaking is prohibited all the way until after the crossing, since the safety of the maneuver can't be judged mid-crossing regardless of the slow vehicle's speed.

On a single-lane two-way road divided by an unbroken line, there is no spare space to stop without blocking the lane opposing traffic needs, so stopping and parking are prohibited even on what would otherwise be the hard shoulder.
Approaching a school or playground is one of the specific situations where the duty of care requires slowing down and becoming more alert, since children may enter the road unpredictably.

A bus traveling in its own designated public-transport lane is passing other traffic within its own reserved lane rather than performing a hazardous overtake of an overtaking vehicle, so it is permitted.

Among the guidance/direction sign series, sign 615 is the overhead sign used to direct traffic through the lanes of an interchange leading onto the freeway, distinguishing it from the other numbered guide signs.

A stop sign posted on the right side of a roadway applies to the whole width of the road approaching it, not just to the lane nearest the sign, so a driver in either lane of a two-lane one-way road must stop.

A vehicle stopped before a level crossing may be waiting because a train is approaching or the tracks ahead aren't fully visible, so overtaking it is forbidden outright, without any exception for road width or line markings.
A portable sign or hand signal given by an authorized member of the road safety guard carries the same legal force as a permanent fixed traffic sign, so drivers are obligated to obey it.
A driver exiting a gas station is entering the roadway from outside it, so the duty is to yield to all approaching vehicles already on the road, from every direction, not just from one side.
For a headrest to properly protect against whiplash in a rear-end collision, its upper edge must be aligned with the upper tip of the driver's head, not lower down at the neck.
The statutory no-stopping and no-parking zone before a pedestrian crossing extends 12 meters, keeping the approach clear so drivers and pedestrians can see one another.

A vehicle legitimately driving within its own designated bus/public-transport lane is passing other traffic inside its own lane, not making a hazardous right-side overtake, so it is permitted to pass on the right.
The general duty of care requires every driver to behave in a way that does not interfere with anyone else's right to make full and lawful use of the road.

A pedestrian crossing is marked by two complementary elements: sign 306, the advance sign warning drivers to give way to pedestrians, and marking 811, the painted zebra-stripe crossing on the road surface itself.

Under vehicle classification rules, a cement mixer is categorized as a commercial truck, since it is a goods/service vehicle fitted with specialized equipment rather than an off-road or special-purpose vehicle.
Vehicle carriers built with three stacked loading levels are granted a specific statutory maximum overall height, including load, of 4.80 meters, reflecting the extra deck's height needs.

Under the Traffic Ordinance's definitions, a lawfully applied road-surface marking is itself legally treated as a road sign carrying full regulatory force, whether or not it's paired with another sign.
A freeway is legally reserved for motor vehicles mechanically capable of and permitted to travel at least 55 km/h, which is why slow-moving vehicles, animals, and pedestrians are excluded from it.
Fog lights are restricted by law to genuine low-visibility weather conditions such as heavy rain, fog, or snow, not for general use whenever a driver finds it convenient.
Israeli traffic law grants the power to revoke a driving license to three distinct bodies acting in their own capacities: the Licensing Authority, a court of law, and the Israel Police.
A traffic separation area is not part of the driving lanes and is off-limits to vehicles by default, with driving on it permitted only when a specific traffic sign expressly allows it.
Roadside vehicle repairs are limited to simple fixes that cause no inconvenience to other road users, and the vehicle may not be left standing there for more than 24 hours.
During the annual vehicle test, the licensing facility must record the odometer reading, documenting the distance the vehicle has traveled as part of the official inspection record.
A driver turning left at an intersection without traffic lights must always yield to oncoming vehicles, since a left turn crosses directly into their path regardless of what those vehicles are doing.

Because the roadway is marked with an unbroken separation line, overtaking remains prohibited even when the opposing lane looks clear, so the correct response is to stay behind the slow-moving wagon at reduced speed.
The default rule for passing a traffic island on a two-way road is to keep to its right side, matching the general keep-right principle, unless a specific traffic sign directs otherwise.

On a narrow road too tight for two vehicles to pass, the vehicle traveling downhill must give way and stop if necessary, since the vehicle climbing uphill has more difficulty regaining momentum once stopped.

A no-left-turn sign restricts turning left specifically; it does not by itself bar a U-turn, which remains governed by the general rule requiring no obstruction to traffic and no other sign or marking that prohibits it.

Overtaking on a steep hill is barred whenever the driver's forward view is limited or obstructed, since safely completing an overtake requires a clear, sufficient sightline, regardless of whether a specific sign is posted.
Overtaking before a pedestrian crossing is prohibited on every type of road, urban and inter-urban alike, because it blocks the sightlines drivers and pedestrians need at that exact point.

Vehicle-marking regulations require an articulated (accordion-style) bus to display rectangular reflective stickers on its rear wall, warning following drivers of the vehicle's extended articulated length.
A flashing green light is a distinct advance-warning phase used to alert drivers that the signal is about to change, specifically indicating it will turn yellow within a few seconds.
The Licensing Authority's power to withhold a license renewal over an unpaid fine is limited specifically to fines that stem from a traffic offense, not any other kind of government debt or penalty.
An accurate oil-level reading requires the engine to be off, so the oil has settled back into the pan, and the vehicle to be on level ground, so the dipstick doesn't give a false high or low reading.
Both alcohol and drugs impair a driver's judgment and reaction ability, amplifying the driver's control limitations in the same way, not just one substance while sparing the other.

Skidding risk peaks specifically when the first rain after a dry spell mixes with accumulated oil and dust on the road, or when mud or oil is already present, since this creates an especially slick surface that sharply cuts tire grip.
Roadworthiness requirements apply year-round, so non-functioning lights, missing windscreen wipers, or tires worn below the legal minimum tread depth are never lawful, even in summer.
A minibus is legally defined by its passenger capacity as a vehicle designed to carry up to 16 passengers in addition to the driver, distinguishing it from other bus classes.
Vehicle classification rules cap a minibus's permitted all-up (gross) weight at 5,000 kg, a threshold that separates it from heavier bus categories requiring different licensing and equipment.
The only recognized exception allowing a motor vehicle (other than an electric vehicle) onto a sidewalk is a vehicle being used specifically to clean the sidewalk.

The law requires any passenger carried on a motorcycle to sit astride it with a leg on each side, since that position is what lets the passenger keep balance and grip the footrests safely, regardless of the road type.
The sudden change in lighting and confined space of a tunnel are specifically listed among the situations requiring a driver to slow down, both at the entrance and throughout the tunnel.
A congested built-up area concentrates pedestrians, parked vehicles, and junctions, all situations specifically listed as requiring a driver to slow down and increase alertness.

An articulated vehicle, whose tractor unit is permanently coupled to a semi-trailer and turns as one unit, is legally distinguished from a separate towing combination, and its statutory maximum permitted overall length is set at 16.50 meters.
Because a double-platform (two-tier) car transporter carries fewer stacked vehicle levels than a three-tier carrier, its permitted overall height including load is set lower, at 4.40 meters.
